newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai king declares Chavalit Yongchaiyudh premier.
newsitem.headline: Thai king declares Chavalit Yongchaiyudh premier.

text.p: Thailand's King Bhumibol Adulyadej on Monday issued a royal decree appointing New Aspiration Party (NAP) leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh the country's 22nd prime minister, the parliament president said.

Wan Muhamad Nor Matha, who is also deputy NAP leader, said the decree, which was issued by the king and delivered to Chavalit's suburban Bangkok home, names Chavalit as the successor to Banharn Silpa-archa in Thailand's top job.

"General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is considered by His Majesty the King as the suitable person to be entrusted with the job of prime minister...His Majesty the King hereby appoints General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh as prime minister...," said Wan Muhamad, reading from the royal decree.
Chavalit, dressed in a white civil servant's uniform, kneeled in front of a portrait of the king to receive the royal decree after it was read out by Wan Muhamad.

Chavalit's NAP won a slim two-seat victory over its rival Democrat Party in the November 17 general election. It has formed a six-party coalition which will command a comfortable majority of 221 seats in the 393-seat parliament.
Pokin Polakun, caretaker minister attached to the prime minister's office, said Chavalit is expected to be sworn in on December 1 along with the members of his cabinet.
